children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to a flat to negative start on September 21, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading lower at around 23,341 in early trade.

The benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty ended mixed on Friday as a drop in crude oil prices was overshadowed by weakness in IT shares and Tata Group stocks.
The Sensex fell 20 points to 74,294.96, while the Nifty gained 75.80 points to 23,346.40. Market breadth remained strong, with 2,531 shares advancing against 1,452 declines.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Down)
GIFT Nifty was trading lower at around 23,341 in early trade, indicating a flat to negative opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Up)

Asian stocks and US equity-index futures advanced with traders looking to a US-China summit later this week for signs of progress on trade between the world’s two biggest economies. Oil fell for a fourth day.
MSCI’s Asia Pacific equities gauge gained 0.2% with South Korean shares leading, while Japan was shut for a public
holiday.
US Equities (Mixed)

Wall Street closed a volatile week on a muted note ​on Friday as benchmark US Treasury yields topped 5%, while crude prices reversed earlier gains but remained above $100 per barrel, keeping inflation worries ‌front and center.

The Dow Jones Industrial ​Average fell 95.40 points, or 0.18%, to 51,682.64, ​the S&P 500 gained 12.74 points, ⁠or 0.17%, to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 104.25 points, or 0.40%, to 26,522.55.
Dollar Index (Flat)
The dollar was quoted in a tight range against Group-of-10 peers in early trading into a week that includes leaders’ meetings during the United Nations General Assembly.
US Bond Yield (Gains)
Expectations for additional Fed rate hikes have pushed investors toward wagers on higher yields in shorter-maturity
debt. The 10-year Treasury yield closed just below 5%.
The yield on 10-year Treasuries and 2-year Treasuries were up 7 and 8 basis points at 4.99% and 4.74%, respectively.
Asian Currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the South Korean won rising 0.194%, followed by the Taiwan dollar (0.157%), Chinese renminbi (0.13%), Malaysian ringgit (0.059%), Japanese yen (0.045%), Singapore dollar (0.024%) and Thai baht (0.015%). Meanwhile, the Indonesian rupiah declined 0.028% and the Philippine peso slipped 0.016%.
Crude (Slips)

Oil prices slid on Monday as investors eyed a recovery in shipments from Saudi Arabia despite ongoing attacks by Yemeni Houthis that have escalated tension in the Middle East while the US and Iran remain in a stalemate.
Brent crude futures dropped 81 cents, or 0.78%, to $103.06 a barrel after settling down 0.91% on Friday.
Gold (Down)
Gold was steady as traders weighed the risk of persistent inflation and the path for interest rates after the Federal Reserve’s first hike since 2023.

Bullion was trading around $4,375 an ounce, after posting a moderate gain the week before. Several Fed policymakers are due to speak publicly this week after voting unanimously to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point at their Sept.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) broke their seven-session selling streak, buying equities worth ₹599 crore on September 18. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to support the market, purchasing equities worth more than ₹1,000 crore during the session.
